1 · Overview

Move 2's scope

Move 2 is the only L0-led Move with continuous cadence in the Lakeshore demo. While Move 0 and Move 1 are per-HoldCo and event-driven, Move 2 runs as a quarterly rationalization slate: AbarVa refreshes the cross-HoldCo vendor view every 90 days, ranks the top 10-20 consolidation opportunities, and presents the slate to Devon Sterling (OP-Finance) and Marcus Rhee (OP-Technology) for ranking, approval, and Source event spawn.

Cadence

Quarterly slate refresh. Mid-quarter delta surfaces when a renewal hits or a new spend baseline lands.

Ownership

L0 OP-Finance (Devon) co-owns with OP-Technology (Marcus). HoldCo CFOs/CIOs consulted, never bypassed.

Output

Ranked slate · per-row action · pre-drafted Source RFP envelope · PortCo socialization comm pack.

Devon's mental model

Devon opens AbarVa Federated Tower → Move 2 every Monday morning at 7:45 AM CT before the L0 ops standup. He sees this quarter's slate, what's moved since last week, what's been approved, what's still draft. He spends 15 minutes ranking unfamiliar rows with Sentinel as his analyst, approves three to four for Source spawn, and forwards the PortCo socialization pack to Kenji (Portfolio Ops). The Source events execute under their own lifecycle; Devon's view in Tower shows the projected → realized rollup on his federated savings ledger.

Sentinel · Move 2 rail

Ask anything about the slate, the scoring, or any vendor row.

Devon Sterling
Why is Workday consolidation ranked 3rd? It's our 3rd-largest line — feels like it should be higher.
Sentinel

Workday lands at rank 3 (score 7.8) because the scoring rubric trades raw savings against disruption and time-to-realize. Three factors pulled it below MS EA and KPMG:

score = 0.45 × net_savings_normalized
− 0.30 × disruption
− 0.25 × ttr_months / 18

1. Net savings band ($0.6–0.9M, 10–15%) is real but smaller in absolute terms than MS EA's $1.0–1.4M.

2. Disruption is Medium, not Low — Roosevelt is mid-rollout and consolidating MSA mid-flight risks Wave 1 stability.

3. TTR is 12 months because Roosevelt's contract doesn't co-term with Morgan Street and Lakefront until Sep 2027.

If Roosevelt's Workday Wave 2 lands ahead of schedule, score recomputes to ~8.4 and Workday jumps to rank 2. I will alert you on the next refresh.

Cited: scoring_rubric_v3.json · loaded vendor_contracts.csv · finserv file 13 IT-spend benchmarks.
Devon Sterling
What's the disruption score made of for CrowdStrike?
Sentinel

CrowdStrike's disruption score (High = 8.5/10) loads on two factors. (1) Concentration risk: all three HoldCos on a single cyber EDR vendor — Move 4 has a standing concentration flag and the 2025 outage exposure made the audit committee skittish. (2) Operational footprint: CrowdStrike is wired into 17 PortCo endpoints and 4 SIEM integrations; swapping is a 6–9 month re-architecture, not a procurement event.

That's why the rubric pushes CrowdStrike to a "split" action rather than "consolidate" — keep CrowdStrike on 2 HoldCos, dual-vendor the 3rd. The savings band ($0.3–0.5M) is paid for by the split, not by single-vendor leverage.

Cited: Move 4 concentration_risk_flag · CIO_bundle.cyber_stack · corpus pattern CYBER-DUAL-VENDOR-2025-Q4.

3 · The vendor normalization view

Before any slate exists, AbarVa de-dupes raw vendor strings across HoldCo APs. Show the matching confidence + human-review queue for low-confidence matches. This is the substrate on which every slate row depends.

Each HoldCo's CIO + CFO bundle includes a vendor inventory. The same legal entity often appears under different strings: "Microsoft Corporation", "MSFT", "Microsoft Online", "Microsoft USA, Inc.". The Move 2 Architecture phase pipeline runs Bronze (raw vendor_raw) → Silver (normalized vendor_entity) → Gold (the slate). The normalization step uses a combination of (a) Dun & Bradstreet DUNS lookups, (b) Tax ID match, and (c) an LLM-judged string similarity over vendor_name + address + last4_tax_id with a confidence threshold of 0.92 for auto-merge.

4 · The opportunity scoring rubric

CFO must understand why the rank order is what it is. The formula is transparent and locked in the Strategy phase memo; changes go through Devon + Marcus sign-off.

score = 0.45 · net_savingsnorm  −  0.30 · disruption  −  0.25 · ttrmonths / 18

All three factors normalized to a 0–10 scale. Final score is a 0–10 number, sorted descending for slate rank.

Factor 1 · Net savings (weight 0.45)

Midpoint of the savings band, normalized by the highest band on the current slate. MS EA's $1.2M midpoint becomes 10/10; CrowdStrike's $0.4M becomes 3.3/10. Why 0.45 weight: this is what the L0 IC cares about most; CFO must see savings drive rank.

Factor 2 · Disruption (weight 0.30)

Composite of (a) operational footprint (how wired-in the vendor is), (b) concentration-risk delta (does consolidation make a flagged risk worse), (c) PortCo blast radius. Scored 1–10, higher = worse.

1–3 Low · paperwork only
4–6 Med · mid-cycle switch
7–10 High · re-architecture
Factor 3 · Time-to-realize (weight 0.25)

Months from approval to realized first-year savings. Capped at 18 months (anything beyond gets max penalty). Anchored on the latest renewal date among incumbent contracts unless an early-term penalty buy-out is cheaper than wait-time NPV.

0–6 mo · fast
7–12 mo · quarterly cycle
13–18 mo · slow

Worked example · MS EA: net_savings_norm = 10.0 (top of slate) · disruption = 2 (Low) · ttr = 6 mo. score = 0.45 × 10 − 0.30 × 2 − 0.25 × (6/18) = 4.5 − 0.6 − 0.083 = 3.82 raw → rescaled to 0–10 across slate → 9.2.

Worked example · CrowdStrike: net_savings_norm = 3.3 · disruption = 8.5 (concentration + footprint) · ttr = 12 mo. score = 0.45 × 3.3 − 0.30 × 8.5 − 0.25 × (12/18) = 1.485 − 2.55 − 0.167 = −1.23 raw → rescaled → 7.1 (still slatable because the action is split, not consolidate, which separately defers the disruption penalty).

5 · Per-category surfaces

Different vendor categories deserve different rationalization approaches. Software (volume + commodity) plays differently than audit (relationship + judgment) than banking (treasury + risk). The slate filters into category views; each view has its own embedded playbook.

Software

Approach: federation + volume leverage. The pure-play is single MSA across HoldCos with tiered commits.

Default action · consolidate to single contract; negotiate enterprise rate at committed spend > vendor's published threshold.
Lever · co-term anchor · bridge offers · competitor stalking-horse RFP.
Benchmark · 10–15% savings on consolidated >$5M spend (finserv file 13, file 20).
Slate rows · MS EA, Workday, Salesforce, Okta, ServiceNow, NetSuite.
Audit + advisory

Approach: federated RFP with scope standardization. Audit firms compete hard on PE-portfolio mandates; relationship + judgment carry weight.

Default action · federated RFP with co-term anchor across all 3 HoldCos. Single firm option + alternates (Deloitte, EY, PwC) as competitive pressure.
Lever · scope harmonization · staffing-tier negotiation · advisory-fee bundle.
Benchmark · 10–15% fee compression on federated audit at >$5M consolidated (corpus pattern AUDIT-FED-2024).
Slate rows · KPMG.
Banking

Approach: rationalize + H2H concentration. Banking is partly Move 0 territory (Morgan Street's L-S01 Banking Consolidation event); Move 2's role is L0-level federation where 2+ HoldCos share banks.

Default action · per-HoldCo Treasurer leads; L0 Move 2 surfaces the federation play (e.g., JPMorgan primary across all HoldCos).
Lever · treasury wallet share · FX volume bundling · H2H-ready selection.
Benchmark · 15–25% fee compression at rationalized concentration (finserv file 08).
Slate rows · (banking is on a separate slate — see L-S01 in Move 0). Move 2 banking work is L0 federation only.
Insurance

Approach: broker consolidation + dual-carrier program. Insurance is the one category where consolidation can increase risk (concentration on a single carrier) — actions skew toward "split" not "consolidate".

Default action · single broker, two-carrier program. Renegotiate broker fee at consolidated premium volume.
Lever · premium-volume tier · broker commission · carrier mix.
Benchmark · 8–12% on D&O / cyber premium federation (corpus INS-PE-FED-2025).
Slate rows · Cyber insurance (Beazley + AIG).
Cyber

Approach: concentration-risk-managed federation. Move 2 + Move 4 jointly own cyber category; concentration risk veto applies.

Default action · if concentration flag green, federate (single EDR vendor at volume rate). If flag amber/red, split or dual-vendor.
Lever · license-tier negotiation · managed-services bundle · threat-intel federation.
Benchmark · 10–17% on EDR + SIEM stack (corpus pattern CYBER-PE-FED-2025).
Slate rows · CrowdStrike (split action recommended due to concentration).

6 · PortCo socialization workflow

Move 2 changes affect PortCos. The L0-led plan must be socialized to PortCo CFOs (not bypassed). The comm + ack flow runs in parallel with Source event execution.

1
Slate approval at L0
Devon + Marcus approve the slate row. AbarVa generates a per-PortCo brief: "your vendor X is part of the federated Q3 slate, action: consolidate. Estimated impact to your P&L: $Y allocated savings. Timeline: see attached."
Trigger
2
HoldCo CFO + CIO read-in
L1 CXOs (Sarah Lindqvist · Daniel Okonkwo at Morgan Street; Priya Naidu · Edward Park at Roosevelt; Marcus Andersen · Yuki Ono at Lakefront) get the brief 48hr before PortCo cascade. They can ack, request edits, or veto with rationale.
Ack required · 48hr
3
PortCo CFO cascade
For each affected PortCo (24 across the portfolio), Kenji Brooks (L0 Portfolio Ops) sends the brief through the HoldCo CFO. Email + AbarVa portal link. PortCo CFO acks or flags operational concerns through the portal.
Cascade · 5 business days
4
Concerns triage
Any PortCo CFO concern routes back to the slate row owner (Devon or Marcus). Two-day SLA to respond; if no acceptable resolution, the row is moved to "Hold" pending re-scoping.
Veto path
5
Source event spawn proceeds
Once all required acks are in (or veto window closed), the Source event spawns. PortCo CFO concerns are attached as context in the Source envelope so the Procurement team can manage operational fit during execution.
Spawn unlocked

Ack telemetry: Devon's Tower view shows per-row ack state — green when all required acks in, amber when waiting, red when a veto is open. The slate row is locked from Source spawn until the ack state clears.

7 · Federated savings ledger contribution

Move 2 outcomes feed Tower Federated's savings ledger (projected → realized). The flow ensures no double-counting and gives the L0 IC a defensible projected-vs-realized view.

Data flow: slate row → Source event → realized savings → ledger

1. Slate approval
Row approved → move_2.slate_row.projected_savings_band writes to federated_ledger.projected with midpoint as the headline number.
→
2. Source spawn
Source event ID stamped on the ledger row. Status moves to "in execution" — Source module owns the variance from here.
→
3. Contract award
Source event closes with awarded contract. Realized savings calculated from awarded fee vs. baseline incumbent fee. Ledger writes realized_y1.
→
4. Quarterly true-up
Quarterly invoice data reconciles realized against projected. Variance surfaces in L0 IC quarterly review. No fake-realized claims.

Source module owns the lifecycle. Once spawned, the Source 11-stage lifecycle (Need → Strategy → Market → RFx → Evaluation → Negotiation → Selection → Award → Contract → Onboard → Realized) runs in the Source module. Move 2 is the originator and the realized-vs-projected reporter in the federated savings ledger, but Devon does not log into Source to manage execution unless he is the explicit signer at the Selection or Award gate.

9 · Empty states

Each pre-bundle state is a designed surface, not blank. The empty states walk Devon from "I just landed in this tenant" to "I have a slate."

State 1 · Pre-bundle-load

No CXO bundles ingested yet for any HoldCo. Move 2 cannot run. Direct Devon to the loader.

"Move 2 needs at least two HoldCos' CIO + CFO + GC bundles to find cross-HoldCo opportunities. Today: zero bundles loaded. Start with Morgan Street — its CFO bundle anchors Move 0 too."

State 2 · One HoldCo loaded · waiting for second

Morgan Street bundles in. Roosevelt and Lakefront pending. Move 2 still cannot rank cross-HoldCo because there is no "cross" yet.

"Morgan Street vendor inventory: 47 vendors, $52M IT spend baseline. Add a second HoldCo to start finding overlaps. Roosevelt CFO bundle takes 4–6 hrs; Lakefront is mature and fastest."

State 3 · Two HoldCos loaded · pre-normalization

Bundles ingested; vendor normalization running. The slate ranker needs normalized vendors before it can score.

"Vendor normalization in progress: 142 raw strings → ~104 normalized entities estimated. Auto-merge running on DUNS + Tax ID; 7 low-confidence matches will route to the review queue. ETA: 18 minutes. Sentinel will notify when ready."

State 4 · Normalization complete · pre-strategy

Vendors normalized but scoring rubric not yet approved. Devon must sign the rubric (Strategy phase) before slate ranks.

"Vendor normalization complete: 104 entities across 2 HoldCos · $42M consolidated spend > $250K threshold. Next: review the scoring rubric draft (Sentinel prepared a default 0.45 / 0.30 / 0.25 weighting; edit and approve to enable slate)."

State 5 · Slate built · awaiting Devon's first ranking session

All 3 HoldCos loaded, normalization clean, rubric approved, slate computed. Default rank order is Sentinel-suggested; Devon can adjust and override.

"Q3 slate ready: 12 rows above scoring threshold. Top 3 by score: MS EA · KPMG · Workday. Suggested approval action: approve top 4 for Source spawn, defer rows 5–6 to PortCo cascade, park rows 7+ to Q4."

State 6 · Mid-quarter delta

Slate was approved at start of quarter; a new signal has arrived (renewal date moved, new vendor spend baseline, M&A added a HoldCo). Show the delta, not a fresh slate.

"Since Jul 1: Workday Roosevelt Wave 2 adoption hit 92% sustained — Workday row score recomputes from 7.8 to 8.4 and now ranks #2. Sentinel suggests reopening the L-S03 envelope. Also: 2 new vendors crossed the $250K threshold (Datadog, Anthropic) and will appear on Q4 slate."

Substrate notes

  • Tenancy: all Move 2 reads require holding_group_id match on the user. L0 sponsor role unlocks aggregate-read across child tenants per the demo shortcut substrate. PortCo writes (ack/veto) scoped to that PortCo's tenant_id.
  • Data plane: Bronze tables vendor_raw populated by loader; Silver table vendor_entity + vendor_normalization_review; Gold view move_2_slate_v3 recomputed nightly + on rubric change.
  • Agent broker boundary: Sentinel rail goes through AgentContextBroker contract — no direct EnterpriseDataRoom or broker / vector / graph imports from the page. Context payload includes selected row id + slate id; broker resolves the vendor + scoring evidence chain.
  • Audit trail: every slate approval, rubric change, veto, and Source spawn writes to move_2_audit_log with actor, timestamp, payload diff. Tower Federated has a per-Move audit view.
  • Source hand-off: spawn API calls /api/source/events/create with envelope payload; Source module is canonical owner from there. Move 2 listens on a Source webhook to write realized_y1 into the federated ledger.

Test coverage targets (Wave 2 spec L06)

  • Unit: scoring rubric math (worked examples for MS EA, CrowdStrike, Workday)
  • Unit: vendor normalization confidence thresholds (auto / review / split boundaries)
  • Behavior: slate row approve → cascade kick-off → Source spawn happy path
  • Behavior: PortCo veto blocks Source spawn until resolution
  • Behavior: mid-quarter delta surfaces but does not auto-recompute approved rows
  • Integration: L0 sponsor sees aggregate, HoldCo CXO sees only own data (RLS)
  • Integration: Sentinel rail responds with cited evidence chain on "why is X ranked Y"
  • E2E: Devon happy-path — open page, drill MS EA, approve, spawn L-S02, see ledger update

11 · Quality bar · the Devon test

Quality bar checklist

Devon opens this page and within 3 minutes:

  • Sees this quarter's top 10 consolidation opportunities ranked · top of canvas, slate is the first thing he sees
  • Understands the scoring at a glance · score bar per row + Sentinel can explain on hover or ask
  • Drills into the top opportunity and reads a one-paragraph "why" · why-panel inside the drill
  • Sees the projected savings range with corpus-cited benchmarks · savings band callout with citations
  • Spawns a Source event with one click · "Spawn Source RFP" big button at the bottom of the drill

If a procurement analyst at any mid-market PE fund opens this page and feels "this is my command center" — that's the target. Datadog-style table density, finserv-style precision, no demo-only handwaving.
